newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul may delay tender offer of New Star.
newsitem.headline: Seoul may delay tender offer of New Star.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board was considering delaying a tender offer for New Star Trading Co by Seoul-based Savoy Hotel, an official at the watchdog body said on Tuesday.

Savoy Hotel last week said it would re-offer to buy an additional 30.81 percent stake in the garment maker at 65,500 won per share after it said it had complied with the watchdog's order in April to reduce its holding in New Star to 22.67 percent.
The official said the Securities Supervisory Board had not yet confirmed that Savoy had reduced its stake. He also said Savoy's documentation of its takeover bid was incomplete.
Savoy told the Korea Stock Exchange in April it would buy 25.3 percent of New Star Trading, which would have been the country's first hostile takeover.

But the Securities Supervisory Board in May had accused Savoy of secretly buying shares of New Star Trading before the takeover bid announcement. The board said the hotel with its affiliate, hotel executives and two others close to Savoy had bought a combined 41.43 percent stake of New Star.

Under South Korean securities regulations put into force on April 1, those who want to buy more than 25 percent of a company's shares are obliged to offer tenders to buy shares until their total stake exceeds 50 percent.

Savoy said last week it had reduced its holding in the garment maker and re-offered to buy 148,592 common shares of New Star Trading in a tender that would open on June 30 and close on July 19 through Ssangyong Securities.
If completed, Savoy with its affiliate and owner family members would be the largest shareholder with a 51.51 percent stake in New Star.
